newsitem.title: USA: Inktomi, NTT to build Internet search for Japan.
newsitem.headline: Inktomi, NTT to build Internet search for Japan.

text.p: Startup Internet technology company Inktomi Corp said Tuesday it has agreed with Tokyo-based Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp to co-develop a search engine for the Japan Internet market.

Inktomi, whose parallel processing technology is behind HotWired's HotBot search engine, said the service would integrate its technology with the InfoBee language analysis software developed by the NTT Human Interface Laboratory.
The Berkeley-based company said the service was expected to be available in the first half of 1996 and that NTT subsidiary NTT Advertising Inc would provide sales and marketing support.
The search engine is due to be incorporated in a number of Japanese sites, including an electronic mall NTT is expected to launch early in 1997.
The entrance to the Japan market of Inktomi follows that of other Internet companies, notably search engine pioneer Yahoo Corp, in which Japanese software distributor Softbank is an investor.
Inktomi also developed the Anzwers search engine for the Australia and New Zealand markets.
